When I first attended AI Camp during the summer of 2022, I could have never guessed how much my life trajectory would change... So, although a bit late, I want to thank everyone and share some of the invaluable knowledge I attained now that I have been involved at AI Camp for over a year! First off, thank you to the teams that constantly motivated me, gave me incredibly insightful information, and refined my skills while teaching me imperative new ones. As a developer/community lead and aspiring product manager, the new perspectives and experiences you gave me were nothing short of phenomenal. ☝️ Michael Ke Zhang , Alex Duffy , Kevin Yen , Jackson C. , Blake Martin , Paul Li, Faris Fakhouri , Gokul Prasad , Jayden Cavanagh , Samuel Hilbert . 🚀 Here are 3 takeaways from my journey: 1. 🧠 New initiatives are only great when you fully understand the 𝘸𝘩𝘺 and 𝘩𝘰𝘸 behind them. Ask yourself: 👉 What does current data show? 👉 What new data needs to be collected? 👉 Does it have a direct tie to increased revenue? If so, what are the individual steps that need to be taken for this initiative to succeed? 👉 Is it the right time to be proposing this? Be detailed and specific, and be able to articulate all of the answers to yourself so you can do the same for others. 2. 👨‍🏫 Perfect your presentation skills. When doing anything in any industry, presentation skills are pertinent. Ensuring you can properly convey, articulate, and pace your ideas alongside why your technical changes matter is highly important, and convincing non-technical individuals that your notions/changes matter relies on this. Remember, most do not understand the technicalities of your work, but they fully understand a 10% or 20% increase in revenue alongside a stunning demo. 3. 📈 If you are a CEO, employees always have to know and believe in the 𝘸𝘩𝘺 for a startup to be successful. If employees simply view work as another task in their day, the journey from 0-100 will likely be grueling and slow. Sure, they will meet deadlines and finish the job, but those who genuinely understand why their individual role matters are going to be motivated to see success, and are ultimately the ones who will drive your company forward. People who see the vision and go out of their way to pick up that new role not because they know it, but because they desire the company to succeed, are the individuals you need to achieve liftoff. You need to constantly value others' work and remind them why it matters/what impact it makes toward the company's ultimate goal; instill a sense of passion into them. --- There are plenty more takeaways, but these were quite important to me and I hope they resonate with you just the same. ⭐️ One last thank you to everyone at AI Camp ! And a special thanks to Chase Adams for being my first mentor at the company. #ai #machinelearning #tech #startup #education #entrepreneurs #intern #internship #aicamp #innovation ...more

Today we’re launching DoorDash Air, our drone program designed and built in-house at DoorDash Labs! We earned Federal Aviation Administration Part 135 air carrier certification, clearing us to operate our own drone delivery service created specifically for local commerce. I believe it’s the next frontier of delivery, and what we’ve learned after years of progress is that you have to solve the full end-to-end system to find out what works and what scales with your customer. The aircraft is one unique challenge, but the bigger problem I’m most excited about is the ground infrastructure: enabling autonomy to work seamlessly inside one of the largest delivery networks in the world. A delivery drone or ground robot is worthless if it doesn't connect a customer who needs something with a local merchant selling it. Across billions of orders and millions of customers, we’ve been purposeful about building our Autonomous Delivery Network with the integration of drones and Dot in a way that helps businesses reach more customers faster. We attract builders. People come here to solve real problems and see their work show up in the physical world, not to sit in R&D hell or in a demo that never moves outside the lab. Read the full story on what we’re building, and if you want to help us solve some of the most interesting problems in autonomy, we’re hiring. ⬇️
